title: A Garden for the Sigil
premise: Mirabel Ravensworth has spent his life as the king's food-taster in a valley where magic cannot enter, swallowing poison so others may feast. When a dying courier presses a sigil-marked map into his hands, the valley's protective nullity shatters and magic floods back in — revealing that Mirabel himself was the seal keeping it out. Hunted by the crown's sorcerers who want their covenant-broken weapon back, he must cross into the realm of the last dragon and reforge the ancient pact between human and magical blood. In the end, Mirabel chooses neither to be the valley's prisoner nor the sorcerers' tool: he plants the sigil as a garden at the border, becoming its living gatekeeper, belonging to both realms and neither.
about_author: Wendell Eriksen is a former botanist turned novelist who spent a decade cataloguing alpine flora before trading field notebooks for fantasy manuscripts. He writes from a cluttered greenhouse office, convinced that every garden is a treaty between wildness and will.

chapters.title: The Taster's Portion
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A routine tasting goes wrong when a dying stranger collapses at the palace gates and presses a sigil-marked map into Mirabel's hands with his final breath. That night, the valley's ageless stillness cracks — flowers bloom out of season, and Mirabel's old scars glow. The emotional beat is dread mixed with a forbidden thrill of wonder, as the man defined by caution feels magic touch him for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Valley Kept Out
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The king's sorcerers reveal the truth: Mirabel was an infant smuggled into the null-valley to smother his dragon-blooded heritage, and the map is the covenant's broken heart. Ordered to surrender it, he flees instead with a disgraced herbalist, Sera, who alone believes him. Crossing the border, magic nearly unmakes him. The beat is terror and betrayal — identity itself revealed as a cage built by others.

chapters.title: The Last Ember
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel, with an interlude from the dragon Vaskarath's memory. In the dragon's ash-choked realm, Mirabel learns the covenant failed because both sides corrupted it — humans hoarded power, dragons demanded worship. The sorcerers arrive to seize the sigil and bind the dying dragon as a weapon; Sera is captured buying Mirabel time. The climax ignites as Mirabel, offered the dragon's full fire, must choose power or repair.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Sigil
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Refusing both theft and vengeance, Mirabel reforges the covenant not as a contract but as cultivation: he plants the sigil in the border-soil, where it takes root as a living garden through which both realms may pass freely. The sorcerers' binding unravels, Sera is freed, and Vaskarath's ember steadies. The resolution's beat is quiet belonging — Mirabel becomes the garden's keeper, finally home on the threshold itself.
